body.payload: Artificial Intelligence in Ecological Monitoring. Researchers across multiple institutions deployed autonomous acoustic sensors to monitor avian biodiversity in temperate rainforests. The deployment spanned three consecutive breeding seasons from 2021 to 2024. Over 12,000 hours of continuous audio were captured across 45 field stations. Automated convolutional neural networks identified 78 distinct species with 94.2 percent precision. The automated approach detected nocturnal vocalizations that human field surveys consistently missed. Environmental variables including ambient temperature and canopy density significantly influenced detection probabilities. The study demonstrates the viability of passive acoustic monitoring at regional scales without physical habitat disruption. The authors make all detection models and labeled acoustic samples freely available under open licenses.
